answer: An applicant posts 350 POA into a public forge escrow, paid from a parent output that has never sponsored another identity. Five randomly sampled established peers form a falcon panel: they recompute the parent outpoint, reject reused or clustered funders, and publish signed uniqueness checks. The bond stays locked through a two-epoch zenith hold; if a shared parent or cloned key is proven, the 350 POA is slashed to those detecting peers. A 100-clone wave therefore risks 35,000 POA and needs 100 unused funding parents, all visible on-ledger.
